newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - London stocks see year out with new record.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - London stocks see year out with new record.

text.p: London, Europe's biggest stock exchange, saw out 1996 by closing at a new record high on Tuesday after a year when many European bourses turned in sparkling performances.

The benchmark FTSE 100 index ended a truncated pre-holiday trading day at 4,118.5, up 2.8 points from Monday's close, itself a record. Most strategists said they were looking for further gains in the new year.
Leading British stocks have chalked up a gain of 11.6 percent in 1996 but were by no means the biggest gainers -- Frankfurt put on 28 percent for the year and the Paris bourse almost 24 percent.

This was dwarfed by Europe's biggest bourse boom in Budapest. There the main BUX index soared 170 percent during the year with analysts citing a swarm of new investors, buying by big funds and good macroeconomic figures after a difficult transition from communism.

On the currency front, the dollar lost momentum and dropped back below 116 yen after touching a 45-month high against the Japanese currency of 116.40. The European currency market is now closed and will reopen for business on January 2.

The dollar slipped after news that November U.S. single-family home sales rose 14.2 percent and December consumer confidence increased to 113.8. The strong data took the dollar down and hit both U.S. treasuries and Wall Street, which was 16 points lower at 6,532 at 1600 GMT.
Dealers said the dollar's bullish undertone was intact despite its late weakness on Tuesday and they believed its end-of-year march against a weakened yen could continue into the New Year.
The yen has been suffering as weak Japanese asset markets reflected general concern about the economic outlook. Traders said the sparse pre-New Year volumes were tending to exaggerate price moves.
"We have seen dollar/yen move up in the last three to four trading days...We have had offers all the way up and I wouldn't be surprised to see it drift higher," said a trader at a Japanese bank.
The dollar also slipped against the German currency after the U.S. data, dropping from firmly above 1.55 marks to around 1.5385 as 1996 London trading closed.
In equities, trading was light in London and Paris, while Frankfurt, along with Amsterdam, Stockholm, Brussels and Tokyo, were closed on New Year's Eve.
According to a Reuters poll, nine of 13 brokerages surveyed predicted London's FTSE would end 1997 above current levels. Estimates were as high as 4,500 and as low as 4,000.

"It'll be a choppy first quarter with political uncertainties coming to a head and then we'll get on with it," said SocGen British equity strategist Andy Hartwill, whose 1997 year-end forecast was 4,250 -- the mean estimate.

In Frankfurt the German stock exchange ended the year on Monday celebrating a record 1996, with not only a 28 percent rise in the main DAX index but also share trading volume up 40.5 percent to 2,434 billion marks ($1,564 billion).
Dealers there said equities were boosted by low interest rates and the successful flotation of Deutsche Telekom, Europe's biggest-ever initial public offering, in November.
The Paris bourse, which soldiered on until its normal 1600 GMT close on Tuesday, ended 2.9 points down, influenced by the weaker tone on Wall Street after a thin trading day.
The blue chip CAC-40 index, which closed the year at 2,315.73 -- still short of its all-time high of 2,360.98 set in February 1994 -- has seen a 23.86 percent recovery over the course of the year.
On the energy markets, winter chills sent oil prices rising again on Tuesday as European buyers rushed to cover seasonal demand while blizzards swept the continent.

London February futures for bellwether North Sea Brent Blend gained 12 cents to close on the last trading session of the year at $23.81 a barrel, boosted by fresh demand, particularly for heating oil in northern Europe.
CURRENCIES AT THE EUROPEAN CLOSE
The dollar closed in Europe around 1.5385 marks and 115.85 yen, compared with 1.5575 and 115.92 late on Monday.
STOCK MARKETS AT THE EUROPEAN CLOSE
The FTSE 100 index of leading British closed 2.8 points up at a record 4,118.5.
In Paris, the CAC-40 share index closed down 2.9 at 2,315.73. The Frankfurt exchange was closed. The 30-share DAX index ended floor trade on Monday at 2,888.69 points.
PRECIOUS METALS

Gold was fixed at $369.55 an ounce, little changed from Monday afternoon's fixing of $369.25 or its close in London of $369.35 on Monday. There was no afternoon fix. Silver was fixed at 479.75 cents, against 488.00 cents previously,
